To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neural crest cells migrate medially to form the roof of a pseudostratified, single cell-layered neural tube.

the neural crest and dorsal midline cells of the neural plate are distinct populations at the onset of neurulation, and that these populations move medially using different forms of cell motility to re-establish the neural tube after fold fusion.

the neural folds are not simply fused together but that cells move from the lateral margins of the neural plate to the dorsal midlines of the neural tube to form the dorsal neural tube and neural crest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the formation of the neural tube and the neural crest.
the mechanisms by which cells move and interact during neural tube formation.
the cellular mechanisms that establish the neural tube and neural crest in vertebrates and the genetic control of these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of a single-cell-layer neural tube from two bilaminar folds requires a combination of cell movements and changes in gene expression.
the dorsal neural folds are not simply fused to form the neural tube, but that the cells of the folds are rearranged to form a single cell layer.

neural crest cells and dorsal neural tube cell populations move to the midline during neurulation by two distinct types of cell motility, and that these cell movements are responsible for re-establishing the neural tube after the neural folds fuse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of the neural tube is a complex, dynamic process involving multiple cell behaviors and gene regulatory networks.
the neural tube is formed by a combination of medial migration and convergent extension of neural crest and neural plate cells, respectively.

the neural tube is formed through a series of cell behaviors including apical constriction of superficial neural cells, rolling of the neural plate, intercalation of lateral deep neural cells, and medial migration of neural crest cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural crest and dorsal tube cells are initially segregated and that their fusion is a consequence of cell motility and not a consequence of changes in gene expression.
neural tube closure in Xenpus involves complex and dynamic cell movements and that the dorsal neural plate cells are not a homogeneous population of cells.
the neural tube is formed from two distinct cell populations, the dorsal neural tube and neural crest, which undergo different forms of cell motility to converge at the dorsal midline.
